actions.justification: MANDATORY: Assess mental status as part of initial DKA assessment. Mental status changes indicate severe DKA and guide management intensity.

MANDATORY: BMP required to check potassium level before insulin can be started (insulin contraindicated if K+ < 3.3 mEq/L), and to assess renal function and electrolytes. Deadline 15 minutes per guidelines.
MANDATORY: Baseline glucose measurement required immediately for DKA management and to guide fluid/insulin therapy. Deadline 15 minutes per guidelines.
MANDATORY action required within 60 minutes per DKA protocol. Serum ketones confirm DKA diagnosis and help assess severity and treatment response.

Per ADA DKA guidelines, IV fluid resuscitation with normal saline (1-1.5L/hr) should be initiated within 15 minutes of presentation. Patient has BP 105/65, HR 108, indicating volume depletion requiring immediate fluid resuscitation BEFORE insulin.

Blood gas is needed to assess pH and bicarbonate level to classify DKA severity (moderate DKA: pH 7.2-7.3, bicarb 10-15), guide bicarbonate therapy decisions, and monitor treatment response. Required per ADA DKA protocol.

BMP has been ordered; per ADA DKA protocol, potassium replacement is required if K+ < 5.3 mEq/L before insulin initiation. DKA patients typically have K+ depletion despite normal/elevated serum levels. Must replace before starting insulin to prevent dangerous hypokalemia.
Anion gap calculation is essential to confirm DKA severity and establish baseline for monitoring resolution. DKA resolution criteria include anion gap ≤12 mEq/L. This helps track treatment response.

Per ADA DKA protocol, regular insulin infusion at 0.1 units/kg/hr should be initiated after potassium replacement is underway and K+ confirmed >3.3 mEq/L. Fluid resuscitation is already started, labs are ordered — insulin is the next critical step to correct ketoacidosis.

Hourly glucose monitoring is required per ADA DKA protocol during insulin infusion. When glucose reaches 200 mg/dL, dextrose must be added to IV fluids and insulin rate adjusted. This is a critical safety monitoring step.

Potassium must be monitored every 2-4 hours during insulin infusion as insulin drives K+ intracellularly, risking hypokalemia. Continuous potassium monitoring is essential to guide ongoing replacement and prevent life-threatening arrhythmias.

Serial anion gap reassessment is required to track DKA resolution. Resolution criteria include anion gap ≤12 mEq/L along with glucose <200 mg/dL and bicarbonate ≥15 mEq/L or pH >7.3. Trending the anion gap guides decisions about insulin infusion and transition to subcutaneous insulin.

Patient has moderate DKA with tachycardia (HR 108), hypotension (BP 105/65), and is 60 minutes into treatment. Serial hydration assessment is essential to guide ongoing fluid resuscitation rates and ensure adequate volume replacement without overload.

Blood gas is pending; if pH <6.9 is confirmed, bicarbonate therapy may be indicated per ADA DKA guidelines. Evaluating this option is appropriate given the severity of presentation with RR 26 suggesting significant acidosis.

Mandatory action - patient has tachycardia (HR 108) and borderline hypotension (BP 105/65, MAP 78). Serial vital sign assessment is critical to monitor response to fluid resuscitation and guide ongoing management.
Mandatory action - IV access must be confirmed/established to ensure reliable route for fluids, insulin infusion, and potassium replacement ongoing in this DKA patient.

Mandatory action - arterial blood gas is required to monitor pH and bicarbonate to classify DKA severity and track resolution. order_lab_blood_gas was completed but order_lab_abg is listed as a distinct mandatory action per this scenario's protocol.

MANDATORY action: Normal saline IV fluid resuscitation is required per ADA DKA guidelines. Despite give_iv_fluid_bolus being completed, start_iv_fluid_ns is the specific mandatory action listed and must be initiated to ensure ongoing fluid replacement at 1-1.5L/hr for this hemodynamically compromised patient (BP 105/65, HR 108).
Labs are pending but anion gap calculation is critical to classify DKA severity and monitor response to treatment. This supports ongoing management decisions.

Assess anion gap closure as part of monitoring DKA resolution criteria (anion gap <=12 mEq/L, bicarbonate >=15, pH >7.3). This is essential to determine when transition to subcutaneous insulin is appropriate.
Labs have been ordered and initial treatment initiated; formally classify DKA severity (moderate based on presentation) to guide disposition and ongoing management intensity.
With hyperglycemia in DKA, corrected sodium should be calculated to guide fluid and electrolyte management.
Moderate DKA with tachycardia (HR 108), hypotension (BP 105/65, MAP 78), RR 26, and active insulin infusion warrants ICU-level monitoring for close hemodynamic and metabolic surveillance.
